act1.label: Act I · Remedial class
act1.title: Spring break, extra lessons
act1.p1: Spring break. Sasaki signs up for remedial class for one reason only: to see his homeroom teacher, Ms. Kawaguchi.
act1.p2: To Sasaki she is more than a teacher. She is the only person who takes his dream seriously, and he worships her almost like a god.
act1.sp1: That dream: becoming an astronaut. Everyone laughs at it except Ms. Kawaguchi, who tells him big dreams are worth chasing with confidence.
act1.boardAria: Classroom chalkboard: spring break, remedial class. Today's assignment: dream big.
act1.pvCaption: Sasaki in class, from the official special PV

chars.name: Sasaki
chars.front: A bespectacled student who joins remedial class only to see his homeroom teacher.

facts.t: Worships Ms. Kawaguchi almost like a god.
Comes to spring-break remedial class just to see his teacher.
Dreams of becoming an astronaut, and gets laughed at for it.
Stands up to an armed man to protect his teacher.
Stops the bullet with his hand, tricks Kuwano with a story about coming from the future, and 20 years later sets foot on the moon.

chars.name: Chieko Kawaguchi
chars.front: The young teacher running remedial class. To Sasaki, she is everything.

facts.t: Kuwano's high-school classmate, who once turned down his feelings.
The only person who doesn't laugh at Sasaki's dream.
The ending hints that she may really be a god.

chars.name: Kuwano
chars.front: The man Ms. Kawaguchi once rejected. He comes to class with a gun.

facts.t: Bursts into the remedial class and opens fire.
Blames that rejection for his ruined life and takes the class hostage.
Believes Sasaki's 'prophecy' about his future and surrenders.

act2.label: Act II · The shot
act2.title: A man walks in and pulls the trigger
act2.p1: In the middle of the lesson a man storms into the classroom, points a gun at the ceiling and fires.
act2.p2: His name is Kuwano, Ms. Kawaguchi's high-school classmate. Years ago, she turned down his feelings.
act2.sp1: Kuwano takes the class hostage. He blames that rejection for his ruined life and makes a vile demand of Ms. Kawaguchi. Sasaki cannot stand to see his "goddess" defiled. He stands up and challenges Kuwano. Kuwano fires.

act3.label: Act III · Time stops
act3.title: The bullet stopped

caps.t: One bullet. A few meters. A fraction of a second.
The title already told us: the bullet stops.
In his palm. Not a scratch.

act3.staticNote: Reduced motion is on: the scene is shown as three still frames.
act3.lie: While everyone stands frozen, Sasaki claims he came from the future, which is how he knew where the bullet would go. Then he "leaks" Kuwano's future: after prison, his life will be a happy one. Kuwano believes him and gives up. Ms. Kawaguchi and the whole class are safe.
act3.sourceNote: This story summary is put together from the official synopsis and several reviews (sources in the wiki). Small details may differ between the manga and the anime.

act4.label: Act IV · The moon
act4.title: Why the moon?
act4.teaser: The 17-21 volume cover and the anime key visual both show a boy in a gakuran uniform on the moon, with Earth behind him. Why the moon? The answer is on the last page.
act4.sp2a: Twenty years later, Sasaki stands on the surface of the moon as the first Japanese person to set foot there. The dream everyone laughed at, except one teacher, came true.
act4.sp2b: The last page hints that Ms. Kawaguchi may really be a god. Did the bullet stop because of Sasaki, because of his "goddess", or because of belief itself? Fujimoto leaves it open.

articles.title: A title that spoils itself
articles.body: The title already tells you the most impossible thing in the story: Sasaki stops a bullet. The tension isn't whether it happens but how and why. 止めた is past tense, so the title reads like a report of something that has already happened.

articles.title: From the Crown contest to Jump+
articles.body:
The story won the Judges' Special Prize (審査員特別賞) in Jump SQ.'s 5th Crown Rookie Manga Award, July 2013 round. The official results page records a judge calling it the most entertaining entry of that round.

It was only published for the public on June 13, 2016 on Shōnen Jump+, as a special one-shot released alongside a Fire Punch update.

articles.title: Drawn at about 20
articles.body: Fujimoto was born in October 1992, so he was about 20 when this story won its contest in 2013. That is why it sits in 17-21: the volume titles are the range of ages Fujimoto was when he drew what's inside.

articles.title: Sasaki is the face of 17-21
articles.body: Of the four stories in 17-21, Sasaki got the cover: a boy in a gakuran leaping across a lime-yellow moon, Earth behind him, orange sky. The anime key visual for this episode deliberately repeats the same composition.

articles.title: Reposted by Fujimoto's "little sister"
articles.body: On October 4, 2021, the day 17-21 came out, the Twitter account ながやまこはる, known as Fujimoto's "little sister", posted this one-shot as a 10-part thread. According to an interview with his editor, the account is actually run by Fujimoto himself.

articles.title: The anime logo: crosshairs inside 弾
articles.body: In the anime's title logo, the inside of 弾 (bullet) is replaced with a crosshair, while 止 (stop) is drawn far larger than the rest, like a wall in the way. This site borrows both motifs: the crosshair cursor and the 止 in Act III.

articles.title: The bullet as the impossible obstacle
articles.body: A bullet is the least negotiable thing there is: fast, straight, lethal. Sasaki stops it not with an explained superpower but with belief. One reviewer reads the bullet as a metaphor for confidence: the impossible gives way when someone truly believes.

articles.title: Faith as a superpower
articles.body: Sasaki treats his teacher as a god, and that faith is what puts him in front of a gun barrel. The story walks the line between comedy and sincerity: the action logic is over the top, but it's delivered with a straight face, as if all of it makes perfect sense.

articles.title: A dream everyone laughs at
articles.body: Sasaki wants to be an astronaut and everyone laughs, except Ms. Kawaguchi. One adult taking a kid's dream seriously drives the whole story, from remedial class to the last page.

articles.title: Worship or humanity?
articles.body: Not every reader likes the premise. The Comics Journal argues that worshipping the teacher as a goddess strips away her humanity, and calls the premise troubling. Top Level Canon finds it less strange and less ambitious than the other stories in the volume. On the other hand, a review on Anitay calls it the best story in the collection. Reading it with both views in mind makes it more interesting.

articles.title: A lie from the future
articles.body: After stopping the bullet, Sasaki doesn't punch Kuwano. He lies: he claims to come from the future and promises Kuwano a good one. The same thing that makes Sasaki strong (believing in something that hasn't happened yet) is used to save everyone, the shooter included.

articles.title: The moon and the Earth
articles.body: Twenty years later Sasaki sets foot on the moon as the first Japanese person there. The bullet's path that froze in Act III continues as a rocket's: same belief, different direction. The last page hints that Ms. Kawaguchi really is a god, and the story never settles which is true.

articles.title: Volume mates
articles.body: In 17-21, Sasaki sits next to Niwatori (2011), Fujimoto's first one-shot about two "chickens" in a schoolyard, plus Love Is Blind (2013) and Shikaku (2014). All four are now episodes of the 17-26 anime too.

articles.title: Love Is Blind, a twin from the same contest
articles.body: The same year, Fujimoto placed in the Crown contest again: Love Is Blind received an Honorable Mention (佳作) in the 9th Crown, November 2013. Two school stories, two chaotic confessions, one year.

articles.title: Straight face, unhinged logic
articles.body: A pattern you'll later feel in Chainsaw Man and Goodbye, Eri is already here: absurd events played completely straight, then an emotional turn at the end that you don't see coming.

articles.title: Lapin Track and the episode 2 team
articles.body: The Sasaki episode was made by studio Lapin Track, directed by Nobukage Kimura, written by Teruko Utsumi, with character designs by Naho Kozono and music by Keiji Inai. The full staff list is in the Anime section.

articles.title: Cast
articles.body: Sasaki is voiced by Toshiki Kumagai, Chieko Kawaguchi by Chika Anzai and Kuwano by Yoichi Okano. In the English dub: Stephen Fu, Brittany Cox and Cory Yee.

articles.title: One episode of eight
articles.body: 藤本タツキ 17-26 adapts eight one-shots from two volumes, one story per episode, by several different studios and directors. Sasaki is episode 2. It had a limited run in Japanese cinemas from October 17, 2025, then went worldwide on Prime Video.
